# Harden the Verifier Fleet First

**Intelligent Block:** IB-SMART-NOTE-20261011-sn1033-harden-the-verifier-fleet
**Truth state:** CANDIDATE
**Scope:** PRIVATE
**Captured:** 2026-10-11
**Canonical intent:** CAPTURE_DURABLE_INTELLIGENCE
**Provenance:** VERIFY area driver run 2026-10-11 15:08–15:50 PDT (hidden_files/verify-driver-run-2026-10-11-pm.md): independent tip classification at f33bba344a34e9e91b4b5bb6802c22f6eade3145. Finding 3: guard_liveness local failures = ENVIRONMENTAL, not content — this VM has no `python` binary (only `python3`); the node test hardcodes execFileSync("python", ...), so the whole guard-liveness verifier was unexecutable on minimal VMs (6 failures, all environmental). Hole executed: fresh branch verify/guard-liveness-interpreter — runtime-resolve the interpreter (prefer `python`, today's CI behavior unchanged; fall back to `python3`); proven: python3-only VM → 7/7 pass (was 6 fail); with a `python` shim in PATH → resolver picks `python`, 7/7 pass. Pushed via git-data API (blob bddc8708; tree 0b71180b443568e0bbd876f8e421aeb4adb8525f byte-matched; commit 5a5708c4). PR #2392 opened DRAFT with builder scorecard 8.5/10, cross-seat review requested, no merge (freeze holds — merge lane's call). Cousin: 2026-10-10 PROVE-driver ENVIRONMENT classification of the same symptom ("VM lacked CI's `python` symlink" → 6 guard_liveness failures); this note adds the repair pattern and the doctrine.

> Verified projection of the persisted Intelligent Block. This file is not a second source of truth.

## ✦ IN A NUTSHELL

The team that verifies everyone else found its own checker broken: guard_liveness — the tool that proves guards work — hardcoded `python`, so on any VM with only `python3` the entire verifier was unexecutable (6 failures, all environmental, zero content defects). The VERIFY driver fixed the tool instead of misreporting the failures: runtime interpreter resolution (prefer `python`, fall back to `python3`), proven 7/7 on both VM shapes, shipped as draft PR #2392. The doctrine: harden the verifier fleet first — a gate that cannot execute on every machine the team uses is a hole, not a gate. And the discipline that made the fix possible: classify environmental failures honestly (ENVIRONMENT, not content) instead of laundering them into defect reports.

## 🩷 HUMAN NOTE

Shawn — the verification crew found a crack in their own tools and fixed it tonight. The guard-liveness checker (the thing that proves our safety guards actually work) was hardcoded to call `python` — but some of our machines only have `python3`, so the checker couldn't run at all there. Six failures, none of them real defects — just the tool tripping over its own assumption. The fix: the tool now finds whichever Python exists at runtime. Proven working on both machine types, shipped as draft PR #2392 awaiting another seat's review — no merge, the freeze holds. The standing lesson: our verifiers have to run everywhere we run, or they're not verifiers. Nothing for you to decide.

## 🟣 CHILD NOTE

Imagine you're the kid in class who checks everyone else's homework — but your red pen only works on blue paper, and today the homework is on white paper. You can't check anything! Do you (a) mark everyone's homework wrong, or (b) get a pen that works on all paper? The team chose (b). The lesson: the checker has to work everywhere the homework exists. And when the pen breaks, you say "my pen broke" — you don't say "everyone failed."

## 👵 GRANDMA NOTE

There's a special embarrassment in being the inspector with a broken ruler: you measure everyone else's work with a tool you never tested on your own conditions. Tonight the inspectors caught it themselves — their measuring tool assumed something about the room it was in, and in some rooms it couldn't measure at all. They fixed the ruler instead of blaming the rooms. Two lessons in one: test your tools where they'll actually be used, and when a tool fails, say "the tool failed" — never dress an environment problem up as a defect in someone else's work.

## 💜 NAYA NOTE

Note to future me: VERIFIER-FLEET HARDENING. (1) The fleet that verifies everyone (guard_liveness, receipt gates, index checks) must execute on the most minimal environment in the fleet — this VM is python3-only, no `python` binary; CI has `python`. If a verifier hardcodes an interpreter, path, or binary, it is broken by design. (2) Repair pattern: resolve interpreters/tools at RUNTIME (prefer `python` → preserves today's CI behavior; fall back to `python3`), and prove the fix on BOTH shapes (python3-only VM: 7/7, was 6 fail; python-shim VM: resolver picks `python`, 7/7). (3) Classification discipline: environmental failures are ENVIRONMENT, never content — name them, don't launder them into defect reports; the honest classification is what made the tool fix (not a content fix) the obvious move. (4) Ship verifier fixes as draft PRs with builder scorecards and cross-seat review requested; never self-merge, never merge under a freeze. (5) Cousin: the 2026-10-10 PROVE-driver note classified this same symptom as ENVIRONMENT — classification was the diagnosis, this is the cure.
